sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Rock County?
sections.html:
Three offices touch a Rock County bill. Your municipal assessor sets the value, the Real Property Description office keeps parcel records, and the Rock County Treasurer collects nearly all of the money. The Treasurer is in the Courthouse at 51 South Main Street, Janesville, WI 53545, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone number is 608-757-5670.

Real Property Description serves every municipality except the City of Beloit and the City of Janesville. That split matters when you move or sell: address changes for Beloit and Janesville go to the Treasurer, and changes for the other 27 municipalities go to Real Property.

The December tax notice tells you where and when to pay. If none has arrived by December 27, call the Treasurer or your local treasurer. The tax is owed whether or not the bill reaches you.

Rock County stretches over 726 square miles on the Illinois border, and Janesville is both the seat and the biggest city. Roughly 71% of homes are lived in by their owners. An estimated 166,472 people lived here in mid-2025, in 72,312 housing units. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $231,600, and gross rent has a median of $1,037. Those numbers give a rough sense of where a typical house will price, though your own assessor's figure and local comparable sales matter more.

Two dates cover most owners, January 31 and July 31, and Beloit adds two more. A bill above $100 may be split, half by January 31 and half by July 31, or paid whole in January. At $100 or under, the full amount is due January 31 (s. 74.11(7) or 74.12). Personal property tax is also due whole on January 31.

  • Everywhere but Beloit: first or full payment January 31, then the second installment July 31, which only the County Treasurer takes.
  • Beloit: four installments, each paid to the County Treasurer.

Through December and January, four towns collect the first payment themselves. Once January 31 passes, the County Treasurer collects for all municipalities, and mailing a check to a local treasurer after that is discouraged.

sections.h2: Late payments and how to pay
sections.html:
Skip one installment and you lose the installment option, with the full unpaid amount turning delinquent. From February 1 the rate is 1.5% monthly, so 18% yearly, and a partial month is billed as a whole one.

Only United States Postal Service postmarks count with the Treasurer, not metered ones. A check mailed on the final day should be hand canceled at the post office counter. Make checks out to the Rock County Treasurer. Cash is taken at the counter only.

  • GovTech Services processes cards and e-checks, charging 2.29% on credit, $3.95 on debit and $1.00 per e-check.
  • To pay by phone, call 1-855-912-7625. Electronic payments can take 5 to 10 business days to arrive.
  • A first payment owed to a town treasurer cannot go through GovTech.
  • One Courthouse drop box sits before security, and another is beside the Treasurer's door on the second floor.

Homeowners with escrow still get the notice. Confirm the lender's payment date, and ask for its tax escrow option notice if you prefer a different one.

Your assessor's valuation notice lists the first protest steps. Dates come from your own clerk, since each municipality schedules its own. The Department of Revenue's Guide for Property Owners and s. 70.47 lay out the statewide process.

  • Raise questions with the assessor at open book. After that, changes require a formal process.
  • The Board of Review sits during a 45-day period that starts the fourth Monday in April, no sooner than seven days after open book.
  • Tell the clerk 48 hours before the first meeting, then submit the signed form PA-115A during the first two hours. The notice can be waived for good cause.
  • You object to land and buildings as one total, and the board presumes the assessor's number is correct until shown otherwise.
  • After a ruling you can appeal to the Department of Revenue (s. 70.85) within 20 days of delivery for a $100 fee, or file in circuit court (s. 70.47(13)) within 90 days.
  • A claim of excessive assessment (s. 74.37) requires that you appeared before the Board of Review first, and it must reach the municipality by January 31 of the year the tax is due.

You can also attend the budget meetings of your school district, technical college, county and municipality, because those budgets set the levy.

Relief here comes from state credits and one loan program, with no separate county exemption. Each agency handles its own applications.

  • Income tax credits through the Department of Revenue: Homestead, Farmland Tax Relief and School Property Tax.
  • Farmland Preservation Credit, from the state agriculture department (DATCP).
  • WHEDA property tax deferral loans for the elderly, 1-800-755-7835.
  • Credits printed on the bill itself: Lottery and Gaming, First Dollar, and School Levy Tax.

Eligibility and deadlines shift, so pick up the current form before counting on a credit in your payoff math.

sections.h2: Before closing on a Rock County house
sections.html:
Ask the Treasurer for what you owe now, with interest, in writing, and pass it to the title company so the closing statement agrees with county records. Owners who are behind keep accruing 1.5% each month until paid.

Names on bills follow deeds. County records reflect the latest recorded document, so a buyer shows up on later bills only once the Register of Deeds has recorded the deed. Walk-ins are welcome there, and the Courthouse lobby has a drop box.

Wisconsin also requires sellers of one to four unit homes to deliver a finished real estate condition report within 10 days of contract acceptance. Without it, the buyer may back out within two business days after the 10 days end (s. 709.02). One part of the form covers taxes, special assessments and permits, so gather those papers first.

Inheriting the house, having tenants or lacking repair money does not change this. Both the tax balance and the report go with the sale however it is structured.

faqs.q: When is the first Rock County property tax payment due?
faqs.a: January 31 is the first deadline. A parcel over $100 can be paid half then and half by July 31, or whole in January. Beloit has four: January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31.

faqs.q: Where do I send Rock County property tax?
faqs.a: Send it to the Rock County Treasurer, 51 South Main Street, Janesville. The exception is a parcel in the Town of Bradford, Janesville, Magnolia or Rock, whose first payment goes to the town. The county takes everything after January 31, and your bill names the right place.

faqs.q: How much interest does Rock County charge on late tax?
faqs.a: The charge is 1.5% a month starting February 1, and part of a month counts as a full one. A single missed installment puts the whole remaining balance in delinquency.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Rock County assessed value?
faqs.a: Start with the steps on the assessor's notice. If open book does not fix it, go to the Board of Review: give the clerk 48 hours' notice and file the objection form early in the first meeting. Dates come from your municipal clerk.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rock County house before the property tax is paid?
faqs.a: Yes, once the unpaid amount is cleared with the Treasurer. A written balance given to the closing agent lets the payoff come out of your proceeds. Chapter 709 also requires the seller's condition report.
